newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end near year high after bonds rally.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end near year high after bonds rally.

text.p: A solid rally in New Zealand bonds helped the share market to a firmer close on Tuesday in healthy trade worth NZ$65 million.

"There was a very good rally in the bonds that underpinned things, coupled with some pretty serious buying orders in the market across the leaders generally," said ANZ Securities broker Duncan Rutherford.

The NZSE-40 Capital Index climbed 14.40 points to close at 2,248.19, just 1.43 points shy of its high for the year. Telecom rose five cents to $6.91, Lion Nathan was seven cents stronger at $3.75, and Carter Holt Harvey was up six to $3.36.
Earlier, New Zealand bonds rallied between three and 12 basis points, with the 11/06 bond yield falling to 8.17 percent.
Brokers said the lower yields had prompted investors to turn their gaze towards equities. Fletcher Forest, an interest rate sensitive stock, gained six cents to $2.11.
New Zealand Oil and Gas, which today announced it had been granted a new oil exploration permit for a 5,500 km area offshore, ended a cent stronger at $0.38.
Rutherford said he saw the market remaining reasonably firm in the short term, even though the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) is expected to hike U.S. rates when it meets tonight (NZT).
"I think a 25 basis point hike (by the FOMC) has been priced into the market to some extent," Rutherford said.
"Anything more than that and we might see things a little differently tomorrow...and if there's nothing, well that would be pretty good too."
